title: Police record 887 dowry murder cases in five years; Odhikar says more than half of 21,627 rape victims since 2001 were girls
excerpt: New figures released as the 16 Days of Activism began show dowry killings and rape cases persist. Nearly half of dowry murder cases were filed in court, not at police stations.

image.credit: File photo: Wasiul Bahar / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
Police have recorded 887 cases of alleged murder over dowry in the past five years, Prothom Alo reported on Wednesday (25 November), citing Police Headquarters data, as the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence began. Separately, rights organisation Odhikar said more than half of the 21,627 rape victims it recorded between 2001 and October 2026 were children, The Daily Star reported.

Of the 887 dowry murder cases, 487 were filed at police stations and the rest in court, according to the police data. Kamarum Munira, assistant inspector general (media) at Police Headquarters, told Prothom Alo that families were often pressured to settle such cases informally and delayed going to the police, so many ended up filing in court.

Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) counted 472 media reports of dowry-related abuse between January 2022 and October 2026, Prothom Alo reported. In these, 220 women were killed and 21 died by suicide; 301 cases were filed. Under the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018 demanding dowry carries one to five years in prison, and causing death over dowry is punishable under Section 11 of the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act 2000.

Odhikar's figures, presented by Sanjida Noor at the Jatiya Press Club on Tuesday (24 November), showed 11,715 of the rape victims were girls and 9,509 women; the age of 403 was not known. Odhikar also recorded 6,815 victims of dowry-related violence since 2001, including 3,748 women killed. It made seven demands, including a victim and witness protection law, speedy trials, measures against online abuse and deepfakes, support for female relatives of victims of enforced disappearance, and withdrawal of Bangladesh's reservations to Articles 2 and 16(1)(c) of CEDAW.

At the same event, Kamrun Nahar of Naripokkho said the women and children affairs ministry has Tk 5,196 crore for 2026-27, of which only Tk 428 crore is for development work, and called for One-Stop Crisis Centres in every district and upazila. Lawmaker Nazmun Nahar cited a BBS survey published in October 2025 that found 76% of women had faced violence from a spouse or partner at least once.

The Odhikar and ASK figures are compiled from media reports and are likely to undercount cases.

Why it matters

The numbers point to the same gap that GBV service providers report: few cases reach the formal justice system, and families face pressure to settle. Legal aid NGOs, shelters and One-Stop Crisis Centres are central to changing that, but the ministry's development budget for this work is small.

What to watch

  • Government and parliamentary commitments during the 16 Days campaign, which runs to 10 December.
  • Progress on a victim and witness protection law.
  • Whether One-Stop Crisis Centres are expanded in the 2026-27 budget revision.

Sources
